summary_paragraph: A male patient was admitted with fever, malaise, and bone pain two weeks after completing treatment for fungal peritonitis following a kidney transplant. He had recently been hospitalized for constipation, which resolved. On admission, he was started on Vancomycin, Zosyn, and Micafungin. Blood cultures remained negative, but urine grew three morphologies of yeast, and beta-glucan was elevated, supporting ongoing fungal infection. Imaging showed a persistent complex perinephric fluid collection, which was aspirated under ultrasound guidance, yielding sanguineous fluid with no growth. After consultation with Infectious Disease, antibiotics were narrowed, and he was transitioned to outpatient IV therapy with Micafungin and a single dose of ertapenem via a newly placed PICC line. His ureteral stents were removed, and home medications were adjusted, including reducing clonidine. He was discharged home with home health support, instructions for weekly labs, and close follow-up with transplant and infectious disease clinics.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
